title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Black Friday Barrel: Chips Charge Back as Stocks Cap Their Best Week in 19 Months
conditions.summary: Stocks rallied across the board in a shortened post-Thanksgiving session, led by a rebound in AI and memory chip names. The S&P 500 rose 1.6 percent and the Nasdaq 2.3 percent, though both are still down for November.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297.49 in a half-day session that ended at noon Central.
The Nasdaq Composite jumped 2.3% to 24,129.50, the Dow added 1.2% to 50,774.94 and the Russell 2000 gained 1.7% to 2,750.30.
AI and semiconductor stocks led a rebound after their recent sell-off, giving the S&P 500 its best week in about 19 months.
Consumer discretionary led the sectors on Black Friday shopping optimism, while utilities and communication services lagged; every sector finished higher.
Even after the bounce, the S&P 500 is down about 3.7% for November and roughly 6.7% below its October record.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: No major US economic reports were scheduled for the holiday-shortened session.
The VIX fear gauge eased to about 24 from just over 28 on Wednesday, well below its 35.89 reading on November 20.
The 10-year Treasury yield sat near 4.9%; sources differed on the day's direction, and the bond market closed early at 1 PM Central.
Gold jumped nearly 4% to around $3,670 an ounce, bouncing off a 14-month low; WTI crude slipped about 0.8% to roughly $83 and bitcoin dipped below $60,000.
The Fed's next policy meeting is December 8 and 9, with no Fed speakers on today's calendar.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: SNDK (SanDisk): +16.0% — memory chip makers led the semiconductor rebound.
BBD (Bradesco): +15.2% — Brazil's president reportedly tapped Bradesco's chairman as finance minister, sparking a rally in Brazilian stocks.
ANT (Anthropic): +11.0% — the newly listed AI company climbed back above its $83 IPO price to $91.88.
KNTK (Kinetik Holdings): +9.3% — reports of a potential acquisition.
MU (Micron): +7.6% — memory and chip names bounced back.
TSLA (Tesla): +5.2% — closed at $400 as growth stocks rallied.
AMZN (Amazon): +4.0% — Black Friday shopping data and AI optimism.
VRTX (Vertex Pharmaceuticals): -5.2% — the FDA extended its review of povetacicept to February 2027.
ALVO (Alvotech): -12.4% — a US court granted Janssen a preliminary injunction against its Simponi biosimilar.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: It was a quiet holiday session with no major earnings reports before the open or after the close.
Earnings pick back up Monday with Chagee before the open and Rubrik after the close.
Next week's big names include Marvell on Tuesday, Salesforce and Snowflake on Wednesday, and Kroger, Dollar General and Ulta Beauty on Thursday.

sections.title: Business News
items: Nvidia rose modestly but remains well below Monday's close, after a week that began with Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO.
Reports said Nvidia Blackwell chips barred from export to China were installed at a Shanghai data center, adding to scrutiny of chip export controls.
Brazilian markets surged after reports that Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi will become finance minister starting in 2027.
Chinese chip stocks posted their biggest one-day gain on record.
Altria said it is considering a cash offer for Imperial Brands, and its shares slipped in early trading.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Monday is next up after the weekend: Chicago PMI at 8:45 AM CT and the Dallas Fed manufacturing index at 9:30 AM CT.
Earnings Monday: Chagee before the open and Rubrik after the close.
Tuesday brings ISM manufacturing and JOLTS job openings at 9:00 AM CT, plus Marvell after the close.
Salesforce reports Wednesday after the close, and the November jobs report lands Friday at 7:30 AM CT.
No Fed speakers are scheduled for Monday; the Fed meets December 8 and 9.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, November twenty-seventh, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down over the water, the turkey leftovers are in the cooler, and we just rode the last set of a short Black Friday session. Gus the wonder dog slept through Thanksgiving dinner, but he is wide awake for the closing bell. Say good evening, Gus! Alright, the final set. The market closed early today, at noon Central, and it was a beauty. The S and P five hundred rose one point six percent to about seven thousand two hundred ninety-seven. The Nasdaq jumped two point three percent to about twenty-four thousand one hundred thirty. The Dow added one point two percent to about fifty thousand seven hundred seventy-five. And the Russell two thousand small caps gained one point seven percent. AI and chip stocks led the charge back after a gnarly sell-off, and every sector finished higher. That gave the S and P its best week in about nineteen months. Consumer stocks led on Black Friday shopping hopes, while utilities lagged. One reality check, though. Even after this swell, the S and P is still down almost four percent for November. Now the wind and weather. There was no big economic data today. The fear gauge, the VIX, eased to about twenty-four, down from just over twenty-eight on Wednesday. The ten year Treasury yield sat near four point nine percent. Gold jumped nearly four percent to around three thousand six hundred seventy dollars an ounce. Crude oil slipped under one percent to about eighty-three dollars, and bitcoin dipped just under sixty thousand. Now let's check the lineup. SanDisk hung ten all the way to the beach, up sixteen percent as memory chips came roaring back. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Micron rode the same wave, up seven point six percent. Brazilian bank Bradesco surged fifteen percent after reports its chairman will become Brazil's finance minister. Anthropic, the big new grom on the block, climbed eleven percent and is back above its IPO price. Kinetik Holdings rose nine percent on buyout reports. Tesla gained five percent to four hundred dollars, and Amazon rose four percent on holiday shopping cheer. On the wipeout side, Vertex fell five percent after the FDA extended a drug review. And Alvotech dropped twelve percent after a court ruling went against it. Tide chart is quiet tonight, with no big earnings in the holiday session. Over on the beach, Nvidia bounced a little but is still below Monday's close, and reports of its banned chips turning up in Shanghai are raising questions. Chinese chip stocks had their biggest one day gain on record. And Altria says it may make a cash offer for Imperial Brands. Tomorrow's forecast, which is really Monday after the weekend. We get the Chicago P M I at eight forty-five A M Central, and Rubrik reports after the close. Tuesday brings the I S M manufacturing report and job openings, then Salesforce reports Wednesday, and the big jobs report lands Friday at seven thirty A M Central. Got a stock, an E T F or a futures contract on your mind? Type it into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. Wax that board for next week, Trade Wind surfers, and catch the Dawn Patrol on Monday morning. This is information, not advice.
